form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Manchin (for himself, Mr. Graham, and Mr. Hickenlooper) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

form.official-title: To require the Secretary of Energy to establish a manufacturing clean energy and energy efficiency grant program, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Manufacturing Clean Energy and Energy Efficiency Act of 2021.

section.header: Manufacturing Clean Energy and Energy Efficiency Grant Program

paragraph.text: The term covered project means a project that—

subparagraph.text: has been recommended in an energy assessment described in paragraph (2)(A) conducted for an eligible entity; and
with respect to the plant site of that eligible entity—

paragraph.text: The term eligible entity means a small- or medium-sized manufacturer that has had an energy assessment completed—

clause.text: a third party assessor that provides an assessment equivalent to that of an Industrial Assessment Center, as determined by the Secretary; and

subparagraph.text: in the 5-year period preceding the date on which the small- or medium-sized manufacturer submits an application under subsection (c).

paragraph.text: The term Industrial Assessment Center means a center located at an institution of higher education that—

subparagraph.text: receives funding from the Department of Energy;
provides an in-depth assessment of small- or medium-sized manufacturers to evaluate the facilities, services, and manufacturing operations of the plant sites of those manufacturers; and
as a result of the assessment described in subparagraph (B), identifies opportunities for potential savings from, with respect to those plant sites—

paragraph.text: The term institution of higher education has the meaning given the term in section 101(a) of the Higher Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 1001(a)).
The term program means the program established under subsection (b).
The term small- or medium-sized manufacturer means a manufacturing firm—

subparagraph.text: the gross annual sales of which are less than $100,000,000;
that has fewer than 500 employees at the plant site of the manufacturing firm; and
the annual energy bills of which total more than $100,000 but less than $2,500,000.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall establish a program within the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy under which the Secretary shall provide grants to eligible entities to implement covered projects.

An eligible entity seeking a grant under the program shall submit to the Secretary an application at such time, in such manner, and containing such information as the Secretary may require, including a demonstration of need for financial assistance to implement the proposed covered project.
In awarding grants under the program, the Secretary shall give priority to eligible entities that—

paragraph.text: have had an energy assessment completed by an Industrial Assessment Center; and
propose to carry out a covered project with a greater potential for—
The amount of a grant provided to an eligible entity under the program shall not exceed $300,000.
A grant awarded under the program for a covered project shall be in an amount that is not more than 50 percent of the cost of the covered project.
A grant received by an eligible entity under the program shall supplement, not supplant, any private or State funds available to the eligible entity to carry out the covered project.

subsection.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $100,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2022 through 2026, to remain available until expended.

section.text: Section 452 of the Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007 (42 U.S.C. 17111) is amended—

paragraph.text: in subsection (a), by adding at the end the following:
The term small- or medium-sized manufacturer means a manufacturing firm—

subparagraph.text: the gross annual sales of which are less than $100,000,000;
that has fewer than 500 employees at the plant site of the manufacturing firm; and
the annual energy bills of which total more than $100,000 but less than $2,500,000.
in paragraph (4), by striking and at the end;
in paragraph (5), by striking the period at the end and inserting ; and; and
by adding at the end the following:

paragraph.text: to provide technical assistance to small- and medium-sized manufacturers, for which the industrial research and assessment center has completed an energy assessment, to upgrade, retrofit, or replace systems or infrastructure consistent with recommendations made in the energy assessment.
